Subject: PulseBridge x Redwood — Prompt observability connector (initial ask)

Hi Aisha,

Quick note to introduce PulseBridge — we do prompt- and token-level observability for LLM flows (traces, prompt diffs, quality signals). Amanda and I discussed a lightweight co-eng to build an official connector for Redwood’s SDKs (LangChain / LlamaIndex adapters + trace propagation).

Attached is a short spec outlining how our trace tags and token-attribution context could be injected at the SDK level, plus a small sample of our trace format. High-level asks:
- Can Redwood expose a hook in the SDK/runtime to accept third-party trace tags and sampling hints?
- Are we able to run an acceptance test on Dedicated or Staging with a small canary?

Attachments: [Attachment: pulsebridge-integration-specs.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: pb-trace-sample.zip (ZIP)]

Happy to sync. Are you available for a 30min tech sync next week?

Best,
Eric Zhao
Head of Integrations, PulseBridge
https://pulsebridge.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eric Zhao <eric.zhao@pulsebridge.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PulseBridge x Redwood — Prompt observability connector (technical read)

Aisha / Vanessa / Eric,

I reviewed pulsebridge-integration-specs.pdf and opened pb-trace-sample.zip. Quick technical notes and questions:
1) Trace model: PulseBridge uses a light JSON envelope with per-token annotations and a sampling header (X-PB-Trace: sampled=1;rate=0.1). We can accept an external header in the runtime gateway; the SDK hooks are straightforward.
2) KV cache tagging: Adding token-level metadata to our internal KV cache traces is feasible but we need to ensure we do not leak customer prompt content to external partners — we will only surface token hashes and attribution scores (not raw prompt text) unless the customer explicitly opts in. That constraint may require a small opt-in flag per deployment.
3) Perf concerns: attaching per-token annotations at high qps adds 3–6% CPU overhead in our microbenchmarks; we should test under a representative workload.

Questions for PulseBridge:
- Can you confirm the minimal schema (we need a trimmed JSON example with hashes only)?
- Do you support a server-side scraping mode (you ingest webhooked summaries) vs real-time header propagation?

Next steps I propose:
- Tech sync to align on schema and sampling semantics (30 min)
- Short performance run in our Dedicated staging (10k requests, 16-token avg)

I can own the perf run if PB can provide a sandbox token and a trimmed schema.

Jonas Weber
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Eric Zhao <eric.zhao@pulsebridge.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amanda Li <amanda.li@pulsebridge.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PulseBridge x Redwood — Prompt observability connector (answers)

Jonas — great notes, thanks. Quick responses inline:
- Minimal schema: attached trimmed-example.json in the repo (see link). We already publish a "hash-only" payload that includes token_sha256, attribution_score, and token_index. We will never send raw prompt text unless explicitly configured.
- Modes: we support both header-propagation (realtime) and async webhook summaries. For initial co-eng we recommend realtime header propagation with a low sample rate.
- Sandbox: Amanda can provide a staging API key and a small wasm-based tracer that inserts X-PB-Trace headers from the SDK.

Repo: https://github.com/pulsebridge/prompt-observability-sdk (see /examples/langchain-adapter)
Drive: https://pulsebridge.ai/sandbox/readme (internal link)

We can take Mon 11/23 10:00 PST for the tech sync. I'll drop a calendar invite.
